title: 恐龙脚印与侏罗纪胖鱿鱼

blocks.en: Hello, young explorers, and welcome back to Michael's Morning Listening! Today our first story begins with one photo on a phone, and with footprints that waited one hundred and twenty million years to be found. Then we dive into an ancient sea to meet the fattest little squid of Jurassic times. Ready? Let's go!
blocks.title: 开场白
blocks.cn: 欢迎回来，小小探险家们，这里是 Michael 的早听晚读！今天的第一篇故事，始于手机里的一张照片，和一串等了整整一亿两千万年才被人发现的脚印。接着我们潜入一片古老的大海，去认识侏罗纪最胖的一只小鱿鱼。准备好了吗？出发！

blocks.en: Our story starts in Phu Phrabat National Park in Thailand. A visitor named Pichai was walking along a small stream when he saw strange, deep marks pressed into the sandstone beside the path. The marks looked like giant footprints. He took a photo with his phone and posted it online with a question: "Do these look like dinosaur footprints to you?"
blocks.title: 恐龙脚印
blocks.cn: 我们的故事发生在泰国的普帕巴国家公园。一位名叫 Pichai 的游客沿着一条小溪散步时，看见小路边的砂岩上压着几个奇怪的深印子。这些印子看起来就像巨大的脚印。他用手机拍下照片，发到网上问大家：“你们看，这像不像恐龙脚印？”

blocks.en: Park rangers came the very next day to measure the marks. Then dinosaur experts studied them carefully — and confirmed the exciting news. The marks are real! They are six footprints of a meat-eating dinosaur, made about one hundred and twenty million years ago.
blocks.title: 恐龙脚印
blocks.cn: 公园的护林员第二天就赶来测量这些印子。随后，恐龙专家仔细研究了它们——并确认了这个令人兴奋的消息：这些印子是真的！它们是一只肉食恐龙留下的六个脚印，产生于大约一亿两千万年前。

blocks.en: There is no skeleton and no bones in the rock — only footprints, like a short message the dinosaur left behind. The soft ground kept the prints, the rock preserved them, and the stream hid them for ages. Only when the water went down did the footprints appear again. Scientists believe the dinosaur was walking here long ago, perhaps looking for food or water. One walk, one photo — and a dinosaur stepped back into the world!
blocks.title: 恐龙脚印
blocks.cn: 岩石里没有骨架、没有骨头——只有脚印，就像恐龙留下的一条短短的消息。松软的地面留住了脚印，岩石把它们保存下来，小溪又把它们藏了很久很久。只有当溪水退下去，脚印才再次出现。科学家相信，这只恐龙很久以前曾在这里行走，也许是在寻找食物或者水。一次散步，一张照片——一只恐龙就这样重新回到了我们的世界！

blocks.en: Now let's meet the belemnites — squid cousins from the time of the dinosaurs. They are extinct today, but their hard inner shells turned into fossils, and scientists find them all over the world. Most belemnite fossils are thin and pointed, like little bullets, only one or two centimetres wide.
blocks.title: 侏罗纪胖鱿鱼
blocks.cn: 现在来认识一下箭石——恐龙时代鱿鱼的亲戚。它们如今已经灭绝，但它们坚硬的内壳变成了化石，科学家在世界各地都能找到。大多数箭石化石又细又尖，像小子弹一样，只有一两厘米宽。

blocks.en: But in Wyoming, in the United States, scientists found a very different one. Its name is Wyoteuthis, and it lived about one hundred and sixty million years ago, in Jurassic seas. Its shell was shaped like a little barrel — and six centimetres wide! That makes it the fattest, chunkiest belemnite ever found. In real life, the animal was about sixty centimetres long.
blocks.title: 侏罗纪胖鱿鱼
blocks.cn: 但在美国的怀俄明州，科学家发现了一只很不一样的。它的名字叫 Wyoteuthis，生活在大约一亿六千万年前的侏罗纪海洋里。它的壳形状像一个小木桶——而且有六厘米宽！这使它成为有史以来发现的最胖、最敦实的箭石。活着的时候，这只动物大约有六十厘米长。

blocks.en: A team from the University of Manchester studied the funny fossil. Some scientists even joke that fossils like this look like "squid butts". A fat little squid, a silly nickname — and a real puzzle for science: why did this one grow so wide, when all its cousins stayed slim?
blocks.title: 侏罗纪胖鱿鱼
blocks.cn: 曼彻斯特大学的一个团队研究了这块有趣的化石。有些科学家甚至开玩笑说，这样的化石看起来像“鱿鱼屁股”。一只胖乎乎的小鱿鱼，一个搞笑的外号——还有一个真正的科学谜题：它的同类都保持着苗条身材，为什么只有它长得这么宽呢？

blocks.en: Here's today's idiom: "follow in someone's footsteps." If you follow in someone's footsteps, you do the same job or the same things as a person who came before you — just like walking in the footprints they left in the ground.
blocks.title: 今日俚语
blocks.cn: 今天的俚语是：“follow in someone's footsteps”（追随某人的脚步）。如果你 follow in someone's footsteps，你就是去做在你之前的人做过的同样的工作、同样的事情——就像踩着他们留在地上的脚印走一样。

blocks.en: The rangers in our story followed in the dinosaur's footsteps, step by step, footprint by footprint! Here is an example: "Lucy's grandmother was a great scientist, and Lucy wants to follow in her footsteps one day." Whose footsteps would you like to follow in?
blocks.title: 今日俚语
blocks.cn: 我们故事里的护林员，正是踩着恐龙的脚印，一步一步、一个脚印一个脚印地追踪它！举个例子：“Lucy 的奶奶是一位了不起的科学家，Lucy 希望有一天能追随她的脚步。”你想追随谁的脚步呢？

blocks.en: Let's think about today's stories. We followed a dinosaur's footprints in Thailand, and we met the fattest little squid of the Jurassic seas. Now here are two questions for you. First: if you found strange, giant footprints beside a stream, what would you do — run away, or take a photo and call a scientist? Second: when you grow up, whose footsteps would you like to follow in? Talk about it with your family!
blocks.title: 结束语与互动问题
blocks.cn: 我们来想想今天的故事。我们在泰国追踪了一只恐龙的脚印，又认识了侏罗纪最胖的小鱿鱼。现在轮到你回答两个问题。第一：如果你在小溪边发现奇怪的巨大脚印，你会怎么做——转身跑开，还是拍张照片、打电话给科学家？第二：等你长大以后，你想追随谁的脚步？和家人聊聊吧！

blocks.en: That's all for today, young explorers. Keep your eyes open on every walk — you never know what is waiting quietly in the rocks under your feet. See you tomorrow morning!
blocks.title: 告别
blocks.cn: 今天的节目就到这里啦，小小探险家们。每次散步都睁大眼睛——你永远不知道，脚下的岩石里正静静地藏着什么。明天早上见！

quiz.title: B. 单项选择（Single Choice）
questions:
How were the dinosaur footprints found?
A. A scientist dug them out of a mountain
B. A visitor took a photo of strange marks and asked about them online
C. Children found them inside a museum
D. Rangers found bones beside a river

What did the experts confirm about the marks?
A. They are footprints of a giant bird
B. They were made by people long ago
C. They are six footprints of a meat-eating dinosaur
D. They are only one hundred years old

How is Wyoteuthis different from most belemnites?
A. It is much longer than the others
B. It has no shell at all
C. It lived in a river, not the sea
D. It is fat and barrel-shaped, six centimetres wide

What does "follow in someone's footsteps" mean?
A. To walk behind someone very quietly
B. To buy the same shoes as someone
C. To do the same things as a person who came before you
D. To draw footprints on the ground

children.text: perhaps looking for food or water
在口语和新闻里常常省略，所以原句里看不到它，但意思一点不少。
（was + 动词-ing）：恐龙走路是"很久以前那段时间正在进行的动作"，不是一个瞬间。用它一下子就有了画面感——恐龙正迈着步子，慢慢走过小溪边。
perhaps looking for food or water
的动作发出者就是前面的恐龙（它在找食物或水）；前面加
（也许），说明这是科学家的推测，不是亲眼所见——新闻报道推测时，这个小词很常见、很严谨。
科学家相信（主干）→ 恐龙当时正在行走（过去进行时，宾语从句）→ 也许在找吃的喝的（分词短语补推测）
。事实和推测分得清清楚楚，这正是科学新闻的说话方式。
